contexts.text: Additionally, we curate a comprehensive benchmark consisting of 812 examples that focus on mapping high-level natural language intents into concrete web interactions. We also offer outcome-based evaluation that programmatically validate the tasks success. Our experiments show that even GPT-4 only achieves a limited end-to-end task success rate of 14.41%, significantly lagging behind the human performance of 78.24%. These findings underscore the need for future research to focus on enhancing the robustness and efficacy of autonomous agents within WebArena environment.   9Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024   ACKNOWLEDGEMENT   We would like to thank Emmy Liu, Zhiruo Wang, Zhitong Guo for examining our annotations, Shunyu Yao for providing the raw Amazon product data in Webshop, Pengfei Liu, Zaid Sheikh and Aman Madaan for the helpful discussions. contexts.text: The main results are shown on the top of Table 2. GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) with CoT prompting achieves a modest end-to-end task success rate of 11.70%, which is signifi- cantly lower than the human performance of 78.24%. GPT-3.5 (OpenAI, 2022) with CoT prompting is only able to successfully perform 8.75% of the tasks. The explicit reasoning procedure is somewhat helpful, it brings 2.34% improvement over the version without it. Further, TEXT-BISON-001 (Anil et al., 2023) underperforms GPT-3.5, with a success rate of 5.05%. These results under- line the inherent challenges and complexities of executing tasks that span long horizons, particularly in realistic environments such as WebArena.   5.1 ANALYSIS   Do models know when to stop? In our error analysis of the execution trajectories, we observe a prevalent error pattern of early stopping due to the model’s conclusion of unachievability. For instance, GPT-4 erroneously identifies 54.9% of feasible tasks as impossible. This issue primarily stems from the UA hint in the instruction, while this hint allows models to identify unachievable tasks, it also hinders performance on achievable tasks. To address this, we conduct an ablation study where we remove this hint.

contexts.text: The negligible correlation demonstrates that the number of interaction rounds has no meaningful relationship with task success.   The analysis reveals negligible correlation (r=-0.028, p=0.916) between episode count and success rate, demonstrating that the number of interaction rounds does not predict task success. GPT-5 Codex leads with the highest success rate ( 44%) while requiring only moderate episode counts ( 10 per trial), followed closely by Claude Sonnet 4.5 ( 43% success, 22 episodes). GPT-5 exemplifies efficiency, achieving 35% success with merely 7 episodes on average. In stark contrast, models like Qwen 3 Coder 480B and GLM 4.5 Air consume significantly more episodes ( 35) yet achieve lower success rates ( 24%). Overall, however, more attempts do not translate to better outcomes. These findings suggest that successful performance in terminal environments depends primarily on the quality of reasoning and decision-making within each interaction, rather than the quantity of attempts.   G.2 OUTPUT TOKEN GENERATION VS. SUCCESS RATE   We collected output token counts for each trial, then calculated the average output tokens per model across all trials to capture the level of verbosity in their approaches. This analysis reveals whether generating more text correlates with better task performance, or if conciseness can be equally effec- tive.
